text.p: Canadians reported a median total income of C$18,900 in 1995, an amount virtually unchanged from a year earlier after inflation was taken into account, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
Before inflation was factored in, the median amount of income reported by Canada's 20.4 million tax filers was C$400 higher in 1995 than in 1994, the federal statistics agency said.
The agency said the gap between men and women narrowed slightly in 1995, as the median total for men slipped while it increased for women.

The national median for men fell to C$25,4000 in 1995 from CC$25,433 a year earlier, with inflation taken into account. For women, the median rose to C$14,500 from C$14,504 in 1994, a rise of 0.7 percent compared with a rise of 4.0 percent in 1994.
Total income includes income from employment, investment, transfer payments, retirement savings and other income.
